findings.current: Hayeon stuck out her tongue and put down her spoon.
findings.defect: The idiom expresses speechless disbelief or exasperation; it does not describe Hayeon playfully sticking out her tongue.
findings.rationale: 혀를 내두르다 conveys being astonished or appalled enough to shake one’s head, so the current version changes her physical reaction and characterization.
findings.replacement: Hayeon could only shake her head in disbelief as she put down her spoon.

findings.current: “Don’t you know Koreans rely on rice power even when they’re about to die? You have to eat if you want your cold to go away faster.”
findings.defect: “Rely on rice power” is an unnatural calque that obscures the familiar claim that Koreans draw their strength from eating rice.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves both 밥심 and the comic 곧 죽어도 exaggeration in natural spoken English.
findings.replacement: “Don’t you know Koreans run on rice even at death’s door? You have to eat if you want your cold to go away faster.”
findings.source: “한국인은 곧 죽어도 밥심인 거 몰라? 먹어야 감기도 빨리 낫는 거야.”

findings.current: *At the very least, one round of circulating qi and breathing would make her feel much better… Huh?*
findings.defect: The established term 운기조식 should be rendered as circulating qi; appending “and breathing” creates an unnecessary literal gloss.
findings.rationale: This follows the binding terminology while preserving the thought that prompts his realization.
findings.replacement: *At the very least, circulating qi once would make her feel much better… Huh?*
findings.source: ‘하다못해 운기조식 한 번이면 훨씬 괜찮아질…… 어라?’

findings.current: “You never listen to me unless you’re willing to die for it.”
findings.defect: The condition is reversed and produces the nonsensical claim that she listens when willing to die.
findings.rationale: 죽어도 안 듣지 means she absolutely refuses to listen, literally that she would not listen even if it killed her.
findings.replacement: “You’d rather die than listen to a word I say.”

findings.defect: “Brat” noticeably sanitizes the narrator’s stronger, profane 이 새끼 reaction.
findings.rationale: The stronger wording preserves Taekyung’s momentary anger and the source’s explicit profanity without intensifying it.

findings.current:
> - [Circulate Qi for Healing] has been completed successfully.
> - [Internal Energy] increases slightly.
findings.defect: The System notices retain square brackets around UI terms, contrary to the required System-panel format.
findings.rationale: The blockquote and System heading already identify the panel; meaningful labels may be bolded but must not remain in square brackets.
findings.replacement:
> - **Circulate Qi for Healing** has been completed successfully.
> - **Internal Energy** increases slightly.

findings.current: “Like I was reborn? Like all the bad energy inside me was washed away. Ugh, I don’t know.”
findings.defect: “Ugh” removes the mild frustrated profanity in 아씨.
findings.rationale: 아씨 is a mild expletive here, not merely a nonverbal groan, and it contributes to Hayeon’s casual sibling register.
findings.replacement: “Like I was reborn? Like all the bad energy inside me was washed away. Ah, damn it, I don’t know.”
findings.source: “다시 태어난 느낌? 내 안에 있던 안 좋은 기운들이 싹 씻겨 내려간다고 해야 하나. 아씨, 모르겠네.”

findings.current: I pushed away the Hayeon who kept asking questions and put my hand into my pocket.
findings.defect: “The Hayeon” is unidiomatic English, and “kept asking questions” loses the importunate quality of 꼬치꼬치 캐묻는.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves both actions and naturally conveys her persistent, probing questions.
findings.replacement: I pushed Hayeon away as she kept peppering me with questions and slipped a hand into my pocket.
findings.source: 나는 꼬치꼬치 캐묻는 하연이를 밀어 내며 주머니에 손을 넣었다.

findings.defect: The item name is unnecessarily enclosed in square brackets despite the binding prohibition on bracketed UI terms.
findings.rationale: Bold formatting already distinguishes the item name within the item window.

findings.current: “I’m just recommending it in case there are any side effects. If you don’t drink it now, you’ll end up spending more money later.”
findings.defect: The current wording presents a tentative recommendation rather than Taekyung’s stated concern, weakening the deliberate lie exposed by the following narration.
findings.rationale: 있을까 봐 그래요 directly gives fear of side effects as his reason, creating the intended contrast with his private admission that there are none.
findings.replacement: “I’m worried there might be side effects. If you don’t drink it now, it’ll cost you more later.”
findings.source: “부작용이 있을까 봐 그래요. 지금 안 마시면 나중에 돈 더 나갈걸요.”

findings.current: Mom hesitated, then took hers first. Hayeon watched her for a moment before following suit.
findings.defect: “Watched her for a moment” omits the pragmatic cue that Hayeon was gauging Mom’s reaction before deciding to follow.
findings.rationale: 눈치를 보던 describes warily reading another person or the situation, not merely looking at her for a duration.
findings.replacement: Mom hesitated, then took hers first. Hayeon cautiously took her cue from Mom and followed suit.
findings.source: 주저하던 엄마가 먼저 포션을 섭취했고, 눈치를 보던 하연이가 뒤를 이었다.

findings.current: “If you have four billion won, then you can spend it like this… Wait, how much did you say?”
findings.defect: The inserted “can” reverses Hayeon’s ongoing criticism into permission to spend recklessly.
findings.rationale: She is still admonishing him for 흥청망청 spending when the amount suddenly registers; the line must retain that negative judgment.
findings.replacement: “Even if you had four billion won, you shouldn’t throw money around like—wait, how much did you say?”

summary: Several action, negation, register, terminology, and formatting errors require correction.
